title: When the Choir Turns Anew
premise: Mirabel Whitlock, youngest guide of the nearly extinct Wayfarers' Guild, is hired to escort a mute pilgrim through the Thornfell passes — only to discover the pilgrim carries a fragment of the old god Veyra, whose return has begun waking prayers across the kingdom. The 'king' on the throne is already hollowed out, worn as a vessel by his chancellor, who bound himself to the dead god Ossivar and fears Veyra's resurrection above all else. As Mirabel's guild loyalty collides with evidence that his own masters helped forge the crown-binding generations ago, he must choose between preserving the Guild's secrets and unbinding the king before the solstice rite completes. In the end, Mirabel sacrifices the Guild's last charter — its claim to legitimacy — to sever Ossivar from the throne, leaving the king mortal, the gods rebalanced, and Mirabel the last Wayfarer, free at last to walk any road he chooses.
about_author: Cyrus Nakamura is a former cartographer who spent six years mapping remote mountain trade routes before turning to fiction, and his novels are prized for their lovingly rendered geography and morally tangled institutions. He writes in a converted waystation cabin and claims every story begins with a road that shouldn't exist.

chapters.title: The Last Charter
chapters.summary: POV: Mirabel. The Wayfarers' Guild, down to nine members, takes one final contract: guide a silent, scarred pilgrim named Sef through Thornfell before winter. Mirabel, proud of roads no one else knows, senses something wrong — birds avoid Sef, and old shrine stones hum when she passes. Emotional beat: quiet pride shadowed by dread of the Guild's coming end.

chapters.title: Prayers That Answer Back
chapters.summary: POV: Mirabel. In a mountain chapel, a dying woman's prayer is audibly answered; Sef weeps for the first time and admits she carries a shard of Veyra, the old goddess of thresholds. Soldiers bearing the king's new seal hunt them by night. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into fear as Mirabel realizes the world's rules have changed beneath him.

chapters.title: What Wears the Crown
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Mirabel and Chancellor Aldous Vane. Captured and brought to the capital, Mirabel glimpses King Edric — and sees the wrongness: eyes like banked coals, a voice that echoes itself. Vane's POV reveals he is Ossivar's vessel, sustaining the binding that keeps Veyra dead. Emotional beat: horror of recognizing power's true face behind familiar authority.

chapters.title: The Guild's Old Sin
chapters.summary: POV: Mirabel. Escaping with help from Guildmaster Corren, Mirabel finds the Guild's sealed archive: the Wayfarers once served as Ossivar's road-wardens, carving the binding into the mountains themselves. His loyalty fractures — the Guild he loves built the cage. Emotional beat: betrayal by inheritance, grief for a heritage built on complicity.

chapters.title: Thresholds and Thieves
chapters.summary: POV: Sef. Fleeing north, Sef's shard grows stronger; through her eyes we see Veyra's memories of the first binding and learn the unbinding requires three threshold-stones, each guarded by what the Guild left behind. Mirabel must betray his oath to open the first vault. Emotional beat: reluctant trust deepening into partnership.

chapters.title: The Road That Remembers
chapters.summary: POV: Mirabel. The second stone lies beneath a smuggler's road that literally remembers every traveler; it forces Mirabel to relive his father's death and his own worst choice — abandoning a client to save himself. He passes only by confessing it aloud to Sef. Emotional beat: shame confronted, self-forgiveness hard-won.

chapters.title: Vane's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV: Aldous Vane. Vane offers Mirabel everything: the Guild restored, charters renewed, his father's name cleared — if he surrenders Sef. For one chapter we inhabit Vane's justifications: he bound himself to save the kingdom from Veyra's wild return. Emotional beat: temptation rendered sympathetic; the reader almost says yes.

chapters.title: Solstice Eve
chapters.summary: POV: Mirabel. Refusing the bargain, Mirabel races Vane's soldiers to the third stone at the Crownspire shrine as the solstice rite begins. Corren arrives — not to help, but to stop Mirabel, believing the Guild's survival depends on the binding holding. Master and apprentice clash on the mountain road. Emotional beat: loyalty weaponized against truth.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Mirabel and Sef. At the shrine, Mirabel uses the charter itself — the Guild's founding covenant — as the final threshold-key, tearing Ossivar out of both the crown and Vane. Veyra rises not as conqueror but as witness; the king wakes in his own body, weeping. Vane crumbles to dust, released. Emotional beat: cathartic climax, sacrifice transmuted into freedom.

chapters.title: Every Road Open
chapters.summary: POV: Mirabel. Spring comes. The king, mortal and diminished, offers Mirabel a court position; the Guild, charterless, dissolves into legend. Sef departs to carry Veyra's word to distant shrines, asking him to come — someday. Mirabel stands at the crossroads below Thornfell, chooses no road yet, and smiles. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution; inheritance replaced by chosen purpose.
